name: Technology — semiconductor_industrial_production_seasonally_adjusted covariate forecasting bundle (monthly)
citation: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis); Yahoo Finance (yfinance)
license: FRED/underlying agencies (Federal Reserve Board G.17 industrial production; BLS PPI; U.S. Census M3 shipments) public data; Yahoo Finance data for research use.
description: Non-EIA, non-benchmark macro/market series (semiconductor industrial production, PPI, Census shipments, and two chip equities). Not a standard forecasting-benchmark corpus, so it does not contaminate model training/eval sources. Long-format TempusBench bundle for application 'covariate_technology_monthly_semiconductor_output'. Target 'semiconductor_industrial_production_seasonally_adjusted' forecast from 4 covariates. monthly cadence, 312 timesteps, 2000-06-01..2026-05-01. NON-EIA (the foundation model is EIA-trained, so EIA sources are excluded). eia_derived=false.
preprocessing: 1. Pull 4 FRED series (IPG3344S, IPG3344N, PCU3344133441, A34HVS) via fredgraph.csv HTTP GET; cache raw CSVs.
2. Parse FRED CSVs: na_values='.'; coerce numeric; normalize observation_date to month-start.
3. Pull TSM & SMH daily adjusted Close via yfinance (auto_adjust=True, start=2000-01-01); cache raw daily CSVs.
4. Resample each equity daily Close to monthly LAST close (resample('MS').last()), labeled at month start.
5. Concat all 6 series on the month-start date key (targets first, then covariates).
6. INNER-join to the common overlap span [max(starts), min(ends)] so no column is missing at the ends (SMH's 2000-06 start binds).
7. Interpolate small internal gaps (<=3 consecutive) linearly; ffill/bfill safety (none needed in practice).
8. Add deterministic known-future covariate month_num from the date.
9. Label dates 'YYYY-MM-01', dedupe, sort ascending; assert monotonic-unique dates and zero NaN; write CSV + meta.
10. Reformatted wide->long TempusBench (variable_name, variable_unit, timestamps, values); timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; variable names expanded; missing->null; values round-trip-verified against source.
11. Removed calendar/time covariates (month_of_year) from the CSV so the only representation of time is the shared 'timestamps' column.

12. Variable names are written in plain English (underscores replaced with spaces). Target — 'semiconductor industrial production seasonally adjusted' (from source column 'semi_ip_sa', unit: index (2017=100)). Covariates — 'semiconductor producer price index' (from source column 'semi_ppi', unit: index); 'electronic component shipments' (from source column 'ecomp_shipments', unit: USD millions); 'tsmc share price' (from source column 'tsm_close', unit: USD); 'vaneck semiconductor etf price' (from source column 'smh_close', unit: USD).

13. Added binary calendar covariates 'is weekend', 'is holiday' (0/1), derived deterministically from the shared 'timestamps' (weekend = Sat/Sun; holiday = US federal holidays). This bundle is monthly (timestamps are month-start dates), so these day-level flags reflect only the 1st of each month and merely reflect the calendar status of that single first-of-month date, not the month as a whole (uninformative here).
14. Removed the calendar covariates 'is weekend' and 'is holiday' from the delivered CSV.
